questions.stem: A projectile is projected with velocity $u$ making an angle $\theta$ with horizontal. What is the angle of elevation of the projectile at its highest point as seen from the point of projection?
questions.solution:
At the highest point, the coordinates are $(R/2, H)$.
The angle of elevation $\phi$ is given by $\tan\phi = \frac{H}{R/2} = \frac{2H}{R}$.
Since $H = \frac{u^2\sin^2\theta}{2g}$ and $R = \frac{u^2\sin 2\theta}{g} = \frac{2u^2\sin\theta\cos\theta}{g}$,
we get $\frac{H}{R} = \frac{\tan\theta}{4}$. Therefore, $\tan\phi = 2 \times \frac{\tan\theta}{4} = \frac{1}{2}\tan\theta$.

questions.stem: A ball is projected from the ground at an angle of $45^\circ$ with the horizontal. After $1\ \mathrm{s}$ it is at its maximum height. The maximum height reached by the ball is $H$ metres. Taking $g = 10\ \mathrm{m/s^2}$, the value of $H$ is _________.
questions.solution:
Time to reach maximum height is $t = \frac{u \sin \theta}{g} = 1\ \mathrm{s}$.
Given $\theta = 45^\circ$, so $u \sin 45^\circ = g(1) = 10\ \mathrm{m/s}$.
Thus $u_y = u \sin \theta = 10\ \mathrm{m/s}$.
Maximum height $H = \frac{u_y^2}{2g} = \frac{10^2}{2(10)} = 5\ \mathrm{m}$.

questions.stem: A projectile is projected with velocity $u$ making an angle $\theta$ with the horizontal. If the velocity of the projectile when it is at its maximum height is $\sqrt{\frac{2}{5}}$ times its velocity when it is at half of its maximum height, then the angle of projection $\theta$ is:
questions.solution:
At maximum height $H$, $v_1 = u \cos\theta$.
At height $h = H/2$, the vertical component of velocity is $v_y = \sqrt{u^2 \sin^2\theta - 2g(H/2)} = \sqrt{u^2 \sin^2\theta - g\frac{u^2 \sin^2\theta}{2g}} = \frac{u \sin\theta}{\sqrt{2}}$.
So, the speed $v_2$ at half the maximum height is $v_2 = \sqrt{v_x^2 + v_y^2} = \sqrt{u^2 \cos^2\theta + \frac{u^2 \sin^2\theta}{2}}$.
Given $v_1 = \sqrt{\frac{2}{5}} v_2 \implies u^2 \cos^2\theta = \frac{2}{5} u^2 \left( \cos^2\theta + \frac{\sin^2\theta}{2} \right)$
$5\cos^2\theta = 2\cos^2\theta + \sin^2\theta \implies 3\cos^2\theta = \sin^2\theta \implies \tan^2\theta = 3 \implies \theta = 60^\circ$.
